introducing.pr_title: feat(server): replace simple CSRF protection with GET method CSRF protection
introducing.pr_body: Adds `GetMethodCsrfProtectionHandlerPlugin`, a zero-config safeguard that makes enabling `GET` on handlers safe with `SameSite=Lax` cookie authentication, and removes `SimpleCsrfProtectionHandlerPlugin` entirely. The new plugin rejects `GET` requests arriving as cross-site or browser-initiated top-level navigations, the only context where another site can make a browser attach explicitly marked `SameSite=Lax` cookies to a safe-method request. Cookie-less cross-site requests keep working, so public APIs need no origin allowlist. ## Behavior - `GET` requests get a `403` before routing when `Sec-Fetch-Site` reports `cross-site` or `none` on a top-level navigation (`Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate` targeting `Sec-Fetch-Dest: document`); a request stripped of either header is rejected rather than passed. - Only `GET` is guarded: navigations can use no method besides `GET` and the unsafe `POST` per the HTML spec, so `HEAD`, `QUERY`, and every other method pass untouched. - Same-origin and same-site requests always pass: the site is the `SameSite` trust boundary, so sibling-subdomain fetches and dev setups need no configuration. - Cross-site `fetch`, ``, `

fix.title: fix(server,contract,ai-sdk): stop loose stacked input schemas from reverting earlier transforms

introducing.head: 4fd063c56de3b9779cfc6d7c0c82dd4bcbb817e5
introducing.sha_method: squash merge commit and its first parent
introducing.pr_title: feat(server,contract,ai-sdk): merge stacked object input schemas
introducing.pr_body:
Multiple `.input()` calls typed as an intersection but validated by piping, so a plain `z.object` stripped the fields the next schema needed. Object input schemas now each validate the original input and the results are merged, so procedure inheritance composes into one flat input without `z.looseObject`.

```ts
const cabinet = authed.input(v.object({ cabinet: v.picklist(cabinetCodes) }))
const operator = cabinet.input(v.object({ operatorId: v.pipe(v.string(), v.uuid()) }))

const update = operator
  .input(v.object({ data: storageWriteDataSchema }))
  .handler(({ input }) => {
    // { cabinet, operatorId, data }
  })
```

### Fixes

- Merging covers the first two levels, so structured inputs like `{ params, query }` compose per group, not just at the root.
- Fields no schema declares are still dropped, so the input stays closed and the client type gains no index signature.
- Middleware sees the fields validated before it, the handler sees them all.
- Non-object values still pipe, so `asyncIteratorObject` and transform chains are unchanged. Loose schemas still pass their extra fields through.
- The request validation plugin and the AI SDK tool input schema follow the same rule, so client and server agree.
- `.output` is untouched, stacking it still needs loose object schemas.

### Notes

Input schemas no longer pipe into each other. That was never expressible in the types, `.input(z.string()).input(z.number())` already infers `never`. Two AI SDK fixtures relied on it and were rewritten.

The merge lives in `mergeTwoLevels` in `@orpc/shared`, shared by the three call sites. It reads own properties only, so `first.__proto__` is not mistaken for an own value.

### Testing

`pnpm test`, `pnpm type:check` and `pnpm lint` pass. The four changed source files are at 100% statement, branch and function coverage.

Closes #1850

pairs.confirm_note: 1851 makes stacked .input() object schemas each validate the original input and merges the results (RequestValidationLinkPlugin: `validating = ... originalInput : currentInput`, same rule in procedure-client and the ai-sdk tool). A later loose schema (z.looseObject, ArkType) echoes the raw value of keys an earlier schema transformed, so the merge reverts the transform. 2099 makes each later schema validate mergeTwoLevels(original, current).
pairs.scope_reason: Wrong value merged in multi-schema validation, a logic error.

bug_card.behaviour: With stacked object input schemas, a later loose schema returns undeclared keys with their raw values, overwriting the earlier schema's transformed values in the merged input; the handler receives untransformed data that contradicts its type.

bug_card.region: packages/contract/src/plugins/request-validation.ts:55 in the PR head, `const validating = inputSchemas.length > 1 && isPlainObject(currentInput) ? originalInput : currentInput`
bug_card.test_gap: Tests merge disjoint strict schemas; none stacks a transforming schema before a loose one, which would fail. The PR body itself says loose schemas still pass extra fields through, a prompt to ask what happens to overlapping keys.

fix.title: fix: stop error-code lookups resolving through Object.prototype

introducing.head: d9d031f90aa2d6e9b256176e6bb16c61058bb2bd
introducing.sha_method: squash merge commit and its first parent
introducing.pr_title: feat(effect): add catchORPCError, catchORPCErrorCode and catchORPCErrorCodes utils
introducing.pr_body:
Adds `catchORPCError`, `catchORPCErrorCode` and `catchORPCErrorCodes` to `@orpc/experimental-effect` for recovering from `ORPCError` failures in an effect's error channel. Recovered errors are excluded from the resulting effect's error channel, and non-matching failures re-fail with their original cause.

## Details

- All utilities support data-first and data-last (`.pipe`) styles, following Effect's `dual` convention.
- Handlers receive the matching errors narrowed from the error channel, with per-code data types preserved.
- `catchORPCErrorCode` and `catchORPCErrorCodes` mirror Effect's `catchTag`/`catchTags` naming and suggest/restrict codes to those present in the error channel.
- Defects and interruptions are not caught.

## Testing

- Logic tests cover all call styles, code matching/mismatch, partial and undefined handler maps, non-`ORPCError` passthrough, defects, successes, and re-failing handlers — 100% statement/branch/function/line coverage on the new module.
- Type tests verify handler narrowing, error-channel exclusion, requirement merging, custom codes, and rejection of out-of-channel codes and map keys.
- Docs: new "Catching ORPCErrors" section on the Effect integration page.

introducing.head: 1074d66231d1de64b6b9aa43de6afbdc6717da5f
introducing.sha_method: squash merge commit and its first parent
introducing.pr_title: feat(snowflake)!: transpilation of Snowflake REGEXP_INSTR to DuckDB
introducing.pr_body:
Adds [REGEXP_INSTR](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/functions/regexp_instr) transpilation for Snowflake to DuckDB.  Since DuckDB lacks a native REGEXP_INSTR function, the position is calculated using: `position = 1 + sum(split_lengths[1:occurrence]) + sum(match_lengths[1:occurrence-1]) + position_offset`

This is done using DuckDB's `STRING_SPLIT_REGEX` and `REGEXP_EXTRACT_ALL` with `LIST_SUM`/`LIST_TRANSFORM` to compute lengths.  Supported parameters:
- `subject` - string to search
- `pattern` - regex pattern
- `position` - starting position (applies `SUBSTRING` offset)
- `occurrence` - which match to find
- `option` - `0` returns start position, `1` returns end position
- `parameters` - regex flags (`i`, `m`, `s`)

`NULL` handling: Returns `NULL` if any argument is `NULL` (matches Snowflake semantics).

Known Limitation
`REGEXP_INSTR` with zero-width anchor patterns like `^` or `$` returns incorrect positions when transpiled to DuckDB due to `STRING_SPLIT_REGEX` splitting between every character instead of at the anchor position.

| Pattern | Input | Expected | DuckDB Result |
|---------|-------|----------|---------------|
| ^       | "abc" | 1        | 2             |

introducing.pr_body:
Replace #22751 

1. only support the default branch in the repository setting.
2. autoload schedule data from the schedule table after starting the service.
3. support specific syntax like `@yearly`, `@monthly`, `@weekly`, `@daily`, `@hourly`

## How to use

See the [GitHub Actions document](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/events-that-trigger-workflows#schedule) for getting more detailed information.

```yaml
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '30 5 * * 1,3'
    - cron: '30 5 * * 2,4'

jobs:
  test_schedule:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Not on Monday or Wednesday
        if: github.event.schedule != '30 5 * * 1,3'
        run: echo "This step will be skipped on Monday and Wednesday"
      - name: Every time
        run: echo "This step will always run"
```

Signed-off-by: Bo-Yi.Wu <appleboy.tw@gmail.com>

fix.title: fix(indexer): index full file paths and real offsets in bleve

introducing.head: 900ac622514081b90e08135cab175d5d1ea1bc9d
introducing.sha_method: squash merge commit and its first parent
introducing.pr_title: Allow code search by filename
introducing.pr_body:
This is a large and complex PR, so let me explain in detail its changes.

First, I had to create new index mappings for Bleve and ElasticSerach as the current ones do not support search by filename. This requires Gitea to recreate the code search indexes (I do not know if this is a breaking change, but I feel it deserves a heads-up).

I've used [this approach](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/7.17/analysis-pathhierarchy-tokenizer.html) to model the filename index. It allows us to efficiently search for both the full path and the name of a file. Bleve, however, does not support this out-of-box, so I had to code a brand new [token filter](https://blevesearch.com/docs/Token-Filters/) to generate the search terms.

I also did an overhaul in the `indexer_test.go` file. It now asserts the order of the expected results (this is important since matches based on the name of a file are more relevant than those based on its content). 
I've added new test scenarios that deal with searching by filename. They use a new repo included in the Gitea fixture. 

The screenshot below depicts how Gitea shows the search results. It shows results based on content in the same way as the current version does. In matches based on the filename, the first seven lines of the file contents are shown (BTW, this is how GitHub does it).

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d938d86-1a8d-4f89-8644-1921a473e858)

Resolves #32096

pairs.confirm_note: The introducing PR's new bleve path token filter built each path prefix with a loop bound that stopped one segment short, so the full file path was never emitted as a term, and it assigned invented start/end offsets. The fix replaces it with a tokenizer that emits real path suffixes with true offsets.
pairs.scope_reason: Off-by-one in token generation and a missing test for full-path search are visible in the diff.

bug_card.behaviour: Path analyzer never produces the complete file path as a token; offsets are fabricated.
bug_card.trigger: Search for a file by its full path such as dir/file.md.

bug_card.test_gap: Filter test asserting the full path term appears for a multi-segment path (the existing test only checked set membership of expected terms and tolerated missing ones).

fix.title: fix(core): remove Bedrock prevalidation from `load`

introducing.head: ebecdddb1b40ef0e8da7f36baa07b4a67c331623
introducing.sha_method: squash merge commit and its first parent
introducing.pr_title: fix(core): add init validator and serialization mappings for Bedrock models
introducing.pr_body:
Adds serialization mappings for `ChatBedrockConverse` and `BedrockLLM` to unblock standard tests on `langchain-core>=1.2.5` (context: [langchain-aws#821](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-aws/pull/821)). Also introduces a class-specific validator system in `langchain_core.load` that blocks deserialization of AWS Bedrock models when `endpoint_url` or `base_url` parameters are present, preventing SSRF attacks via crafted serialized payloads.

Closes #34645

## Changes
- Add `ChatBedrockConverse` and `BedrockLLM` entries to `SERIALIZABLE_MAPPING` in `mapping.py`, mapping legacy paths to their `langchain_aws` import locations
- Add `validators.py` with `_bedrock_validator` — rejects deserialization kwargs containing `endpoint_url` or `base_url` for all Bedrock-related classes (`ChatBedrock`, `BedrockChat`, `ChatBedrockConverse`, `ChatAnthropicBedrock`, `BedrockLLM`, `Bedrock`)
- `CLASS_INIT_VALIDATORS` registry covers both serialized (legacy) keys and resolved import paths from `ALL_SERIALIZABLE_MAPPINGS`, preventing bypass via direct-path payloads
- Move kwargs extraction and all validator checks (`CLASS_INIT_VALIDATORS` + `init_validator`) in `Reviver.__call__` to run **before** `importlib.import_module()` — fail fast on security violations before executing third-party code
- Class-specific validators are independent of `init_validator` and cannot be disabled by passing `init_validator=None`

## Testing
- `test_validator_registry_keys_in_serializable_mapping` — structural invariant test ensuring every `CLASS_INIT_VALIDATORS` key exists in `ALL_SERIALIZABLE_MAPPINGS`
- 10 end-to-end `load()` tests covering all Bedrock class paths (legacy aliases, resolved import paths, `ChatAnthropicBedrock`, `init_validator=None` bypass attempt)
- Unit tests for `_bedrock_validator` covering `endpoint_url`, `base_url`, both params, and safe kwargs

pairs.confirm_note: The fix removes the Bedrock SSRF prevalidation as a policy decision (keep provider policy out of core), not because the introducing PR's validator was defective.

fix.title: fix(langchain): sanitize cache settings for fallback models

introducing.head: 4cdd47b253d78a4987f1e0aec51b78948c2e8b09
introducing.sha_method: squash merge commit and its first parent
introducing.pr_title: fix(langchain): sanitize anthropic cache markers on fallback retries
introducing.pr_body:
## Summary

Fixes #33709.

When `AnthropicPromptCachingMiddleware` runs before `ModelFallbackMiddleware`, Anthropic-specific `cache_control` markers can leak into fallback attempts targeting non-Anthropic models. This change makes fallback retries sanitize those markers only on non-primary attempts, preserving primary-call behavior and avoiding API changes.

Related: langchain-ai/deepagentsjs#551.

## Changes

### libs/langchain_v1

- Added a private fallback sanitizer in `model_fallback.py` to remove Anthropic `cache_control` markers from fallback requests.
- Sanitization covers `model_settings`, system/content message blocks, and tool payloads (`BaseTool.extras` plus dict-style tools/extras).
- Applied sanitization in both sync and async fallback retry paths (`wrap_model_call` and `awrap_model_call`) while leaving the primary attempt unchanged.

### libs/langchain_v1 tests

- Added sync and async regression tests in `test_model_fallback.py` that simulate primary failure and assert fallback calls only succeed when cache markers are stripped.
- Verified non-cache settings (for example `temperature` and `top_p`) are preserved on fallback.
- Preserved existing fallback behavior coverage (ordering, exhaustion, and error propagation).

## Compatibility with `BedrockPromptCachingMiddleware`

The sanitizer also covers `BedrockPromptCachingMiddleware`, which injects `cache_control` into `model_settings` only. Bedrock-specific markers (`cachePoint` blocks, content-block `cache_control`) are applied by the chat model classes at API-call time and never appear in the `ModelRequest`, so no additional handling is needed.

pairs.confirm_note: The fix extends fallback sanitisation to additional providers' cache settings (Fireworks, prompt_cache_key); the introducing PR correctly handled the Anthropic markers it targeted, so this is a follow-up extension.
pairs.scope_reason: New-provider feature gap, not a flaw in the original lines.

fix.title: Fix `pydantic-ai-ui-security-review` workflow: drop invalid `needs:` under `on:`

introducing.head: e558325989f34a3dab3f16b9b08fcbe869445393
introducing.sha_method: squash merge commit and its first parent
introducing.pr_title: Gate `pydantic-ai-ui-security-review` behind a maintainer click-to-start approval
introducing.pr_body: > **Proposal for @strawgate's review** — this reshapes one of the gh-aw workflows you own > (`pydantic-ai-ui-security-review`). Nothing here is final; the job-graph wiring in particular is > yours to sign off on. It compiles on the **current pinned gh-aw `v0.74.8`** — no version bump. ### What this changes and why Today `pydantic-ai-ui-security-review` auto-runs on every push to any PR that touches the UI paths — an expensive AI run firing on every commit. This makes it **manual and approval-gated** using a GitHub **Environment with required reviewers**, and (once the repo-admin steps below are in place) lets a UI-touching PR be **blocked from merging until the review has been started and run**. The shape: - **Runs on every PR** (the trigger's `paths:` filter is removed). A new cheap, no-AI **`detect`** job applies the same UI-path list and outputs whether the UI security surface was touched. - **Non-UI PR** → the agent is skipped via `if:` → its check reports **`skipped` = success**, so it never blocks merge. No AI, no approval prompt. - **UI PR** → the `activation` job references the **`ui-security-review`** Environment, so the run **pauses** showing a **"Review deployments → Approve"** button. A maintainer clicks Approve to **start** the AI review. While pending, the agent's check stays pending → **merge is blocked** until the review has run. `synchronize` is kept so a new commit re-reports the check and re-pends the approval. `tests`, `coverage`, `lint` and every other check are **completely untouched** — this is a separate workflow with its own check context; making it manual/gated can't block or obscure them. ### How the gating is wired (the part for @strawgate) The intuitive approaches don't compile cleanly on `v0.74.8`, so I used the gh-aw-native combination that does (details + the dead-ends in `local-notes/design-report.md`, happy to walk through): - **`on.needs: [detect]`** makes `detect` a *pre-activation* dependency, so the top-level **`if: needs.detect.outputs.touched == 'true'`** (which gh-aw copies onto the `activation` + `agent` jobs) references a real dependency rather than a non-dependency. - **`on.manual-approval: ui-security-review`** puts the Environment gate on `activation`. Because `activation` is itself gated by the `if:` above, **approval is requested only on UI PRs** (a skipped job never requests Environment approval) — so `manual-approval` here is *not* the "gates every run" footgun it would be on its own. Why not the alternatives: - **Top-level `environment:`** stamps the gate onto `pre_activation` too, which has no `if:` and runs on every PR → it would prompt for approval on *non-UI* PRs. - **A custom downstream `approval_gate` job** referenced via the top-level `if:` produces an invalid `needs.` reference on `activation` (or a dependency cycle), because custom jobs sit downstream of `activation` while gh-aw applies the `if:` *to* `activation`. I verified the compiled graph is **cycle-free** and every `if:` reference resolves to a real dependency. The lockfile diff is only this change — no `ERR_CONFIG`/domain/import drift. **One side effect to flag:** none from this approach (top-level `environment:` would have suppressed gh-aw's secret-validation step; `on.manual-approval` does not). The `detect` job lists the UI paths in one regex — if that list drifts from the security surface, update it there. ### Not in this PR (David's repo-admin steps, separate) - Create the **`ui-security-review`** Environment with **required reviewers** (maintainers / a team). - Mark the security-review **agent job's check** as a **required status check** in branch protection for the merge-gate to take effect. The workflow's `description:` still says *"pydantic-ai-pr-review owns the merge-gate verdict until gh-aw check-runs land"* — left as-is for you to update if you adopt this gate. ### Checklist - [ ] Any **AI generated code** has been reviewed line-by-line by the human PR author, who stands by it. - [x] No **breaking changes** in accordance with the [version policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/version-policy.md). - [x] **PR title** is fit for the [release changelog](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/releases).

pairs.confirm_note: The introducing PR added a needs key under the workflow's on block, which is not valid there, so GitHub rejected the whole workflow on every run. The fix removes it and recompiles, with the detect dependency already expressed at the job level.
pairs.scope_reason: CI workflow config / compiler quirk.

fix.title: fix(auth): avoid "compromised account" false-alarm when login with remember-me token

introducing.head: c6c829fe3fde5d55b2115eb006b427288e381158
introducing.sha_method: squash merge commit and its first parent
introducing.pr_title: Enhanced auth token / remember me
introducing.pr_body:
Closes #27455

> The mechanism responsible for long-term authentication (the 'remember me' cookie) uses a weak construction technique. It will hash the user's hashed password and the rands value; it will then call the secure cookie code, which will encrypt the user's name with the computed hash. If one were able to dump the database, they could extract those two values to rebuild that cookie and impersonate a user. That vulnerability exists from the date the dump was obtained until a user changed their password.
> 
> To fix this security issue, the cookie could be created and verified using a different technique such as the one explained at https://paragonie.com/blog/2015/04/secure-authentication-php-with-long-term-persistence#secure-remember-me-cookies.

## :warning: Breaking

The now obsolete setting `[security].COOKIE_USERNAME` has been removed.
If you previously set it, you can now remove it from your config.

pairs.confirm_note: The remember-me token rotation replaced the token hash on every auto-login and treated any stale cookie as a compromised token, so two near-simultaneous requests with the old cookie raised a false alarm. The fix remembers the previous hash and allows a short grace window.
pairs.scope_reason: Concurrency/timing of in-flight cookies.

introducing.head: 0b680ec41203815757876c39613eb4d53037f2c8
introducing.sha_method: squash merge commit and its first parent
introducing.pr_title: fix: update internal `$ref`s in renamed schema `defs`, handle missing keywords, and detect semantically different defs
introducing.pr_body:
## Summary

This PR fixes three bugs in `merge_json_schema_defs` and `_update_mapped_json_schema_refs` in `pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/_utils.py`:

### Bug 1 (Critical): Internal `$ref`s in renamed definitions not updated

When `merge_json_schema_defs` renames a `$def` due to a name collision, only the top-level schema's `$ref`s are updated via `_update_mapped_json_schema_refs`. The renamed definition's own internal `$ref`s are **not** updated.

**Example:** Schema A defines `Outer` and `Inner`. Schema B also defines `Outer` and `Inner` but with different structures, where `Outer` references `Inner`. After merging, Schema B's defs get renamed to `Outer_1` and `Inner_1`. However, `Outer_1` still contains `{"$ref": "#/$defs/Inner"}` instead of `{"$ref": "#/$defs/Inner_1"}`, creating a broken cross-reference that points to Schema A's `Inner` instead of Schema B's `Inner_1`.

**Fix:** After building the `schema_name_mapping`, iterate over *all* definitions from the schema (not just renamed ones) and update their internal refs, since a non-renamed def can also reference a renamed def.

### Bug 2: `_update_mapped_json_schema_refs` misses `additionalProperties`, `allOf`, and `not`

The function recursed into `properties`, `items`, `prefixItems`, `anyOf`, and `oneOf`, but missed three standard JSON Schema keywords:

- **`additionalProperties`** — used for `dict[str, SomeModel]` or models with extra fields
- **`allOf`** — used for model inheritance / intersection types
- **`not`** — used for negation constraints

Any `$ref` nested under these keywords would be silently skipped during ref rewriting.

**Fix:** Added handling for all three keywords in `_update_mapped_json_schema_refs`.

### Bug 3: Structurally equal defs with different `$ref` targets silently merged

The equality check `def_schema != all_defs[name]` compares raw dict structure including `$ref` strings. Two defs that are structurally identical (same `$ref` strings) but whose `$ref`s resolve to different actual types (because the referenced defs differ between schemas) were incorrectly treated as duplicates and merged.

**Example:** Schema A has `Inner={type: string}` and `Wrapper={$ref: Inner}`. Schema B has `Inner={type: integer}` and `Wrapper={$ref: Inner}`. Both `Wrapper` defs are structurally identical, so Schema B's `Wrapper` is silently dropped. But after merge, Schema B's `Wrapper` now incorrectly resolves to Schema A's `Inner` (string) instead of Schema B's `Inner` (integer).

**Fix:** After building the initial name mapping, check defs that were considered "equal" for `$ref`s that would be remapped. If applying the mapping changes the def, create a separate renamed copy with updated refs. Loop until stable to handle transitive chains (A→B→C where only C was renamed).

## Test plan

- [x] Verify existing tests pass (no regressions in ref rewriting behavior)
- [x] Test with schemas where renamed `$def`s contain internal cross-references
- [x] Test with non-renamed defs that reference renamed defs
- [x] Test with schemas using `additionalProperties`, `allOf`, and `not` containing `$ref`s
- [x] Test with structurally equal defs whose `$ref`s resolve to different types

pairs.confirm_note: The introducing PR added a fixpoint loop that marks a shared def as kept under its own name as soon as it is visited, so a def processed before its dependency gets renamed stays wrongly shared and the result depends on $defs order. The fix collects shared defs first and only keeps them after the fixpoint converges, also copying defs instead of mutating inputs.
pairs.scope_reason: Order-dependent control flow in the added loop is visible from the diff.

introducing.pr_title: feat(core): add `reasoning_effort` as a standard chat model parameter
introducing.pr_body:
`langchain-anthropic`, `langchain-openai`, `langchain-fireworks`, and `langchain-xai` now support a standard `reasoning_effort` parameter. It can be set at model construction or per invocation, with each provider translating it to the appropriate API. 
 `ModelProfile` now exposes supported reasoning effort levels and the default level for supported models.

---

Adds a standard `reasoning_effort` parameter across chat model integrations. Like `temperature`, it can be set on the model or per call, while each provider translates it into its own API format.

Motivating example: [`deepagents-code` (dcode)](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/code/overview) implemented provider-agnostic reasoning effort itself. This PR upstreams that support into LangChain's provider integrations, making `reasoning_effort` a standard parameter and exposing supported levels via `ModelProfile`.

```python
from langchain_anthropic import ChatAnthropic

model = ChatAnthropic(model="claude-sonnet-4-6")
model.invoke(
    "Why do parrots have colorful feathers?",
    reasoning_effort="high",
)
```

### Model specific labels and default

| Provider | Model / version | Levels supported | Default |
|----------|-----------------|------------------|---------|
| **OpenAI** | gpt-5.5, gpt-5.6* | `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` (+ `max` on gpt-5.6+) | `medium` |
| | other gpt-5* | `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` | — |
| **Anthropic** | Opus 4.0 / 4.1 | *(none – predates effort entirely)* | — |
| | Opus 4.5 | `low`, `medium`, `high` | `high` |
| | Opus 4.6 | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `max` | `high` |
| | Opus 4.7+ | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` | `high` |
| | Sonnet 4.0 / 4.1 / 4.5 | *(none – predates or rejects effort)* | — |
| | Sonnet 4.6 | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `max` | `high` |
| | Sonnet 5+ | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` | `high` |
| **Fireworks** | DeepSeek V4 Pro | `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` | `high` |
| | Kimi K2 | `low`, `medium`, `high` | — |
| | GLM 5 | `none`, `high`, `max` | `max` |
| **xAI** | Grok 4.5-class models | `low`, `medium`, `high` | `high` |

### Provider specific details

| Provider | Model class | Translation |
|----------|-------------|-------------|
| **OpenAI** | `ChatOpenAI` | Translates `reasoning_effort` to `reasoning.effort` and adds `summary: "auto"`. |
| **Anthropic** | `ChatAnthropic` | Translates `reasoning_effort` to `output_config.effort` and defaults `thinking` to `adaptive`. |
| **Fireworks** | `ChatFireworks` | Sends `reasoning_effort` as a flat field unchanged. |
| **xAI** | `ChatXAI` | Nests `reasoning_effort` under `extra_body.reasoning_effort`. |

### Anthropic: `effort` alias

`ChatAnthropic` already exposed an `effort` parameter. This PR makes it a true Pydantic alias for `reasoning_effort` while preserving existing behavior.

- Both `effort` and `reasoning_effort` work at construction; if both are provided, `effort` wins.
- Call-time (`.invoke()`, `.bind()`) support is handled manually to preserve the same precedence, since Pydantic aliases only apply at construction.
- `effort` remains supported (no deprecation).

### Other providers

- **DeepSeek**: inherits support from `BaseChatOpenAI`.
- **Groq** and **Perplexity**: already have native `reasoning_effort` support.
- **OpenRouter** and **Mistral AI**: out of scope (no native support today).
- **Google (Gemini)**: implemented separately in [`langchain-google`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-google/pull/1895)

## Summary

When extended thinking is enabled and the model returns text alongside a tool call, the text is discarded in favor of executing the tool. If the model then responds with only `ThinkingPart`s (nothing more to say), that response previously fell through to the retry prompt ("Please return text."), forcing the model to duplicate its earlier text.

This PR consolidates the empty-response and thinking-only-response handling into a single "no actionable output" block that:

- Checks `finish_reason == 'length'` (raises `UnexpectedModelBehavior`) for both empty and thinking-only responses
- Checks `finish_reason == 'content_filter'` for empty responses only
- Attempts backward-looking text recovery from a previous `ModelResponse` (e.g. text that was discarded alongside a tool call)
- Falls back to empty-request resubmission (empty responses) or the retry prompt (thinking-only responses) when no text is recoverable

The text recovery logic is extracted into a `_recover_text_from_message_history` static method on `CallToolsNode`.

introducing.pr_title: Install skills flat by Name, not namespaced InstallName
introducing.pr_body:
## Problem

Most agent clients (Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, etc.) only discover **immediate subdirectories** of their skills folder. When a skill repository uses namespaced paths like `skills/author/my-skill/`, the installer was creating nested directories (e.g. `.claude/skills/author/my-skill/`) that clients could not find.

Reported by users: skills from repos with structure like `skills/<namespace>/a-skill/` install to `<agent>/skills/<namespace>/a-skill/` instead of `<agent>/skills/a-skill/`, and the client doesn't recognize them.

## Solution

Separate the skill's **identity** from its **filesystem path**:

- **`InstallName()`** (unchanged) - returns `namespace/name` for namespaced skills. Used for lockfile keys, search, filtering, display, and update matching.
- **`Name`** - the plain skill name, now used for the install directory. Skills are always installed flat:

```
.claude/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md       # correct (flat)
.claude/skills/author/my-skill/SKILL.md # was wrong (nested)
```

## Changes

| File | What changed |
|------|-------------|
| `installer.go` | Use `skill.Name` for directory paths instead of `InstallName()` |
| `install.go` | Use `skill.Name` for overwrite checks and prompts |
| `collisions.go` | Detect conflicts by `Name` since flat install means two skills with the same Name but different Namespace collide |
| `update.go` | Clean up old namespaced directories when updating migrates to flat layout |
| Tests | Updated to reflect flat install behavior and collision detection |

## Validation

- The [agentskills.io specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) defines skills as flat folders (`skill-name/SKILL.md`)
- Agent clients scan only first-level subdirectories of their skills directory
- All existing tests pass; lint clean

The fix stages and swaps contents in place.

introducing.pr_title: perf(browser): pre-bundle the vitest runtime in optimizeDeps
introducing.pr_body:
Pre-bundles the vitest runtime for browser mode so the browser fetches a few optimized chunks instead of ~20 separately-served dist chunks (faster startup, fewer module requests).

`vitest`, `vitest/internal/browser` and `@vitest/browser/client` are moved from `optimizeDeps.exclude` to `include`. They are optimized together in a single pass, so esbuild dedupes their shared stateful chunks (the test collector, the runner, the RPC client) to a single instance — preserving module identity between the test files' `import 'vitest'` and the tester. Their transitive deps (`@vitest/utils`, `@vitest/spy`, `pathe`, `tinyrainbow`, …) are inlined into these bundles. The virtual per-server modules (`@vitest/browser/context`, …), `vite/module-runner` and `msw` must stay excluded (see the comment in `index.ts`).

**Shared-server resolver fix.** The `vitest:resolve-core` plugin (`vitestResolver.ts`) short-circuits bare `vitest` imports straight to the running copy's dist file. It now lives on the single Vite server shared by every environment, so it also governs the browser `client` environment where the runtime is pre-bundled — without care the tester would use the optimized bundle while test files receive the raw dist graph, producing two `@vitest/runner` instances and failing every `test()` with "Vitest failed to find the current suite". When the environment includes `vitest` in `optimizeDeps`, the plugin now routes the import through the optimizer (`this.resolve`) so both share one instance; every other environment keeps the pinned dist resolution.

Stack frames pointing into the optimizer cache (`.vite/vitest`) are ignored in stack traces like the un-bundled `/vitest/dist/` ones. The console-logging spec now runs with an explicit `default` reporter and asserts on Vitest's own console forwarding: once the runtime is pre-bundled the tester loads a stubbed `@vite/client`, so Vite's client console relay no longer runs.

pairs.confirm_note: The introducing PR moved vitest into browser optimizeDeps and patched only one of the two resolver plugins, so with inline projects the root resolver still sent imports to raw dist files, creating a second runtime copy. The fix keeps both resolvers out of the browser client environment and excludes the unresolvable browser client entry from pre-bundling.
pairs.scope_reason: Bundler/module-resolution interplay across plugins not visible in the diff.

introducing.pr_title: fix(fireworks): translate canonical multimodal content blocks for chat completions
introducing.pr_body:
## Summary

`langchain_fireworks._convert_message_to_dict` ships LangChain canonical v0/v1 multimodal content blocks (e.g. `{"type": "image", "base64": ..., "mime_type": ...}`) on the wire unchanged. Fireworks' OpenAI-compatible chat completions API rejects the unknown `base64`/`mime_type` keys and the list shape on roles that expect a string, returning HTTP 422 — so any image upload, including via tools that return image content blocks, fails for Kimi K2.6 and other Fireworks vision models.

This change mirrors `langchain_openai.chat_models.base._format_message_content`:

- Walk `content` blocks.
- Drop block types the chat-completions wire doesn't carry (`tool_use`, `thinking`, `reasoning_content`, `function_call`, `code_interpreter_call`).
- Detect v0/v1 multimodal data blocks via `langchain_core.messages.is_data_content_block`, and translate them via `convert_to_openai_data_block(..., api="chat/completions")`.
- Strings and non-list content pass through unchanged.

Applied in the `ChatMessage`, `HumanMessage`, `SystemMessage`, and `ToolMessage` paths of `_convert_message_to_dict`. `AIMessage` already routes through `_convert_from_v1_to_chat_completions` for v1 output and assistant content is text-only on the way out, so it is left untouched.

## Why this approach

Fireworks is OpenAI-compatible. The canonical → OpenAI translator already exists in `langchain_core.messages.block_translators.openai` and is the same one `langchain-openai` uses. Reusing it (rather than inventing a Fireworks-specific translator) gives:

- v0 (`source_type`-based) and v1 (`base64`/`url`-based) data block coverage for free.
- Consistent behavior with `langchain-openai` for image, file, and any future canonical data block.
- A small, focused diff (≈30 lines of new code, plus tests).

## Test plan

- [x] `make test` passes (64/64 unit tests, including 9 new ones for the new helper and translation paths).
- [x] `make lint` passes (ruff check, ruff format, mypy, lint_imports).
- [ ] End-to-end: image upload to a Kimi K2.6 (Fireworks) agent translates to `{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,..."}}` on the wire and the model returns a coherent description (validated locally against `langchain-fireworks==1.0.0` site-packages with the same patch).

introducing.pr_title: fix(dbos,prefect): preserve runtime `toolsets` in durable runs
introducing.pr_body:
- Closes #6075

### Summary

This PR fixes the same runtime `toolsets=` override bug in two durable wrappers:

- `DBOSAgent`
- `PrefectAgent`

In both wrappers, the durable override context replaced the agent's effective toolsets with only the constructor-time durable toolsets. Because the base agent ignores per-run `additional_toolsets` whenever toolsets are already overridden, runtime `toolsets=` were silently dropped inside durable runs.

That broke cases like runtime `ExternalToolset` usage, where the model should be able to return `DeferredToolRequests` for externally-executed tools.

The fix is the same in both wrappers:

- merge constructor-time durable toolsets with per-run `toolsets=` inside the wrapper override context
- keep passing `toolsets=toolsets` through `run()` / `run_sync()` so the runtime toolsets still reach `iter()`
- pass `toolsets=None` from the durable wrapper's `iter()` into `super().iter()` because the merged override is already active there, avoiding double-application

### Why Temporal Is Not Changed

`TemporalAgent` is intentionally different.

Inside a Temporal workflow, runtime toolsets are explicitly rejected today and covered by tests/docs. That wrapper pre-registers durable activities for its model/tool execution surface up front, and the worker/plugin model depends on those activities being known ahead of workflow execution.

So this PR only fixes the wrappers where runtime toolsets are intended to work but were being dropped accidentally.

### Verification

- Added a DBOS regression test for runtime `ExternalToolset` support in `tests/test_dbos.py`
- Confirmed that test fails without the DBOS fix and passes with it restored
- Added a matching Prefect regression test in `tests/test_prefect.py`
- Verified the Prefect behavior with a direct runtime repro returning `DeferredToolRequests(...)`
- `tests/test_prefect.py` is currently blanket-skipped upstream, so the Prefect verification could not rely on the module test runner yet

### Checklist

- [x] Any **AI generated code** has been reviewed line-by-line by the human PR author, who stands by it.
- [x] No **breaking changes** in accordance with the [version policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/version-policy.md).
- [x] **PR title** is fit for the [release changelog](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/releases).

fix.title: fix discovery support in nested dirs

introducing.head: eaa018545aff23f22744a0faade18b58c5c4aaf2
introducing.sha_method: squash merge commit and its first parent
introducing.pr_title: Add --allow-hidden-dirs flag to gh skill install
introducing.pr_body:
## Description

Adds `--allow-hidden-dirs` flag to `gh skill install` to support discovering skills in hidden (dot-prefixed) directories such as `.claude/skills/`, `.agents/skills/`, and `.github/skills/`.

### Motivation

Some repositories publish skills exclusively under hidden directories (e.g. `.claude/skills/`). The current discovery logic only looks in standard conventions (`skills/`, `plugins/`, root-level `*/`), so these repos appear empty to `gh skill install`.

We want to be **less strict** about where skills can live, but we do not want to fall back to pure recursive parsing of arbitrary directories. Hidden-dir discovery uses the **same structured conventions** as standard discovery, just rooted under a dot-prefixed host directory:

- `.{host}/skills/*/SKILL.md` (hidden-dir)
- `.{host}/skills/{scope}/*/SKILL.md` (hidden-dir-namespaced)

This keeps discovery predictable and convention-based while supporting real-world repos.

### Why this is opt-in

Hidden directories are typically **installation targets** (where consumers store skills) rather than **publication roots** (where publishers share skills). Skills found in these directories may be committed copies from another publisher, making attribution unclear. Keeping this behind a flag:

- Preserves the distinction between publishing and consuming
- Warns users that skills found in hidden dirs may be redistributed copies
- Unblocks users who need to install from repos that only publish in hidden dirs

### Architecture

**Discovery layer returns all skills; callers decide filtering.** Following review feedback, the discovery package no longer references CLI flags:

- `DiscoverSkillsWithOptions` / `DiscoverLocalSkillsWithOptions` always return **all** skills (standard + hidden-dir)
- `DiscoverSkills` / `DiscoverLocalSkills` (convenience wrappers) auto-filter hidden-dir skills for backward compatibility with `preview`, `update`, and `publish` commands
- The `install` command applies `--allow-hidden-dirs` flag logic via `filterHiddenDirSkills()`, showing a clear error when hidden skills exist but the flag is not set

### UX

**Error when hidden skills exist but flag is not set:**
```
no standard skills found, but 3 skill(s) exist in hidden directories
  Use --allow-hidden-dirs to include them
```

**Warning when `--allow-hidden-dirs` is set:**
```
! Skills in hidden directories (e.g. .claude/, .agents/) may be installed
  copies from another publisher. Verify the skill's origin and check for a
  canonical source.
```

### Example

```bash
# Without flag - clear guidance
$ gh skill install mrgoonie/claudekit-skills
no standard skills found, but 45 skill(s) exist in hidden directories
  Use --allow-hidden-dirs to include them

# With flag - discovers and warns
$ gh skill install mrgoonie/claudekit-skills --allow-hidden-dirs
! Skills in hidden directories (e.g. .claude/, .agents/) may be installed
  copies from another publisher. ...
? Select skill(s) to install:
> [ ]  [hidden-dir] aesthetic
  [ ]  [hidden-dir] ai-multimodal
  [ ]  [hidden-dir] backend-development
```

Works with both remote repos and `--from-local`.

Fixes #13197

Related: https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/192851

pairs.confirm_note: The flag PR deliberately limited hidden-directory discovery to the repository root and the fix widens it to any depth and adds exact nested-path handling, which is an extension of the feature rather than a defect in the added lines.
pairs.scope_reason: Feature extension, not a defect.

Changes:

@tool("structured_api", response_format="content_and_raw_output")
def _mock_structured_tool_with_raw_output(
    arg1: int, arg2: bool, arg3: Optional[dict] = None
) -> Tuple[str, dict]:

    return f"{arg1} {arg2}", {"arg1": arg1, "arg2": arg2, "arg3": arg3}


def test_tool_call_input_tool_message_with_raw_output() -> None:
    tool_call: Dict = {
        "name": "structured_api",
        "args": {"arg1": 1, "arg2": True, "arg3": {"img": "base64string..."}},
        "id": "123",
        "type": "tool_call",
    }
    expected = ToolMessage("1 True", raw_output=tool_call["args"], tool_call_id="123")
    tool = _mock_structured_tool_with_raw_output
    actual = tool.invoke(tool_call)
    assert actual == expected

    tool_call.pop("type")
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        tool.invoke(tool_call)

    actual_content = tool.invoke(tool_call["args"])
    assert actual_content == expected.content

introducing.pr_body:
## Description

Fixes an issue in the `accepts` helper where `defaultMatch` failed to match wildcard media types (`*/*` and `type/*`, e.g., `application/*`) sent by clients in `Accept` headers against server-supported MIME types.

### Problem
`defaultMatch` previously used a strict `supports.includes(accept.type)` check. When clients sent standard browser wildcard headers like `Accept: application/*` or `Accept: */*;q=0.8`, `defaultMatch` failed to match supported MIME types like `application/json`, inappropriately falling back to the `default` MIME type.

### Solution
1. Added `matchType` helper function to handle exact matches, subtype wildcards (`application/*`), and global wildcards (`*/*`).
2. Added `getSpecificity` ordering so exact MIME matches take precedence over wildcard matches at the same quality factor (`q`) level per RFC 9110 HTTP Content Negotiation semantics.
3. Updated `defaultMatch` to sort preferences by quality factor (`q`) and specificity before resolving against supported server media types.

## Checklist
- [x] Added unit tests for `application/*`, `*/*`, and specificity ordering.
- [x] All unit tests pass (`npx vitest run src/helper/accepts/accepts.test.ts`).
- [x] Type checking passes clean (`npx tsc --noEmit`).

introducing.pr_title: Restore typed values in a dynamic tool's Temporal `ActivityConfig` after the activity round trip
introducing.pr_body: - Closes #6896 A `DynamicToolset`'s tools are discovered inside the get-tools activity, so their `ToolDefinition.metadata` returns to the workflow as JSON. Everything typed in the tool's `ActivityConfig` degrades on the way back — `timedelta(minutes=5)` becomes `'PT5M'`, a `RetryPolicy` becomes a plain dict, an `ActivityCancellationType` becomes an int — and the workflow then hands that to `workflow.execute_activity`. That's a workflow-*task* failure, which Temporal retries forever, so the workflow never reaches a terminal state. ### Reproduced, not just read New end-to-end test `test_durability_dynamic_tool_timedelta_activity_config_survives_round_trip` runs a real workflow against a real dev server, with the dynamic toolset passed at construction time so it really is wrapped (`@agent.toolset` registers too late — that's #6902). Against unpatched `main` it produces exactly the reported failure and then hangs until the workflow's `execution_timeout`: ``` AttributeError: Fail to convert to Duration. Expected a timedelta like object got str: 'str' object has no attribute 'seconds' .../temporalio/worker/_workflow_instance.py:3054 in _apply_schedule_command v.start_to_close_timeout.FromTimedelta(self._input.start_to_close_timeout) ``` The test carries a short `execution_timeout` on purpose, so a regression fails the test rather than hanging it. I also found a second, earlier failure mode on the same round trip that the issue didn't mention: a round-tripped `retry_policy` reaches `with_non_retryable_errors` as a dict and raises `AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'non_retryable_error_types'` before `execute_activity` is even reached. Same class, same fix. ### The fix (option 2, and it restores everything) `resolve_tool_activity_config` now validates the resolved config through a `TypeAdapter(ActivityConfig)` before handing it on. The issue guessed this "won't restore all of them" because `ActivityConfig` holds non-Pydantic types; measured against temporalio's actual `ActivityConfig`, it restores **every** field: | field | wire value | validated back to | |---|---|---| | `start_to_close_timeout` etc. | `'PT5M'` | `timedelta` | | `retry_policy` | dict | `RetryPolicy` | | `cancellation_type` | `0` | `ActivityCancellationType` | | `versioning_intent` | `1` | `VersioningIntent` | | `priority` | dict | `Priority` | A fully-populated native config validates to an equal config, so statically-configured tools are unaffected. Option 1 (a typed field on `DynamicToolInfo`) was rejected: `DynamicToolInfo` is the engine-agnostic dataclass in `durable_exec/_toolset.py`, and giving it a Temporal `ActivityConfig` field would leak one engine's types into the shared wire format. **Option 3 is folded in rather than done separately.** Per @DouweM's comment, failing loudly beats livelocking. Anything validation *can't* restore now raises a `UserError`, which is in `workflow_failure_exception_types` and so fails the workflow instead of retrying the workflow task forever. That includes a misspelled key: `extra='forbid'` is set deliberately, because without it validation would silently drop the typo that `workflow.execute_activity(**config)` currently rejects (loudly, but as a livelock) — so this direction is strictly better than both the old and the permissive behaviour. Validation lives in `resolve_tool_activity_config`, the single place that reads per-tool Temporal config, so the MCP get-tools activity — which round-trips `ToolDefinition`s the same way — is covered by the same code path rather than a second special case. ### Tests - `test_durability_dynamic_tool_timedelta_activity_config_survives_round_trip` (end-to-end workflow; fails on `main` with the reported `AttributeError`) - `test_resolve_tool_activity_config_restores_round_tripped_types` - `test_resolve_tool_activity_config_rejects_unusable_config` Full `tests/test_temporal.py` passes (207 passed, 2 skipped). ### Checklist - [ ] Any **AI generated code** has been reviewed line-by-line by the human PR author, who stands by it. - [x] No **breaking changes** in accordance with the [version policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/version-policy.md). - [x] **PR title** is fit for the [release changelog](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/releases).

### Description

<!--

background they need before the problem makes sense, and avoid jargon.
-->

The automated Go update stopped working when Go 1.27 was released. The workflow first installed the Go version already listed in `go.mod` (Go 1.26), then changed `go.mod` to require Go 1.27. When it ran `go mod tidy`, the command correctly refused to continue because the installed toolchain was too old.

This changes the update flow so it prepares and validates the complete upgrade before opening a pull request:

1. Refuse to run when tracked changes are already staged or unstaged, protecting local dry runs from accidentally committing and discarding existing work.
2. Ask `setup-go` for the latest stable release, then pass the exact installed version into the bump script. The script no longer resolves Go independently, so release propagation cannot make setup and the update target disagree.
3. Install the latest golangci-lint release that can validate that Go version.
4. Update `go.mod`, run `go mod tidy`, and apply any source migrations from `go fix`.
5. Run the full test suite and linter. If either fails, restore the original clean worktree, remove the temporary branch, and stop without creating a pull request.
6. If everything passes, commit all tracked changes and open the Go update pull request.

After `go mod tidy` normalizes the final Go directives, the generated pull request updates `.github/workflows/lint.yml` only when Go still differs from the starting state. It records the exact golangci-lint version used during validation, giving a new Go major a compatible linter while keeping normal pull request and trunk CI on a reproducible version pin. A newer linter or a temporarily redundant toolchain directive cannot create a linter-only pull request.

This pull request only changes the automation. Any Go 1.27 source migrations and the corresponding linter pin will be produced and reviewed together in the follow-up Go update pull request.

### Description

Make the `fsModuleCache` resilient to external modifications and avoid returning stale cache references that no longer exist.  This is an issue for long-lived CI workers that perform periodic disk space maintenance.

- `ensureCacheIntegrity` wrote the metadata file unguarded, before any test ran, so an unwritable cache directory aborted the whole run.
- `cacheResult` awaited an unguarded `saveCachedModule`. A failed write rejected the module fetch. Catching it is not enough on its own: the result handed back is a pointer to the cache file, so the fallback has to serve the module inline instead of pointing the worker at a file that was never written.
- `getCachedModule` short-circuited on `__vitestTmp` without checking the file still existed, so a worker that failed to read a stale cache file got the same dangling pointer back on every retry. The worker now retries once, and the server drops the stale result and re-transforms.

introducing.pr_body:
Adds an optional `when` predicate to `InterruptOnConfig`, allowing dynamic per-tool-call control over whether a HITL interrupt fires.

---

**`when` predicate in `InterruptOnConfig`**

```python
class InterruptOnConfig(TypedDict):
    allowed_decisions: list[DecisionType]
    description: NotRequired[str | _DescriptionFactory]
    args_schema: NotRequired[dict[str, Any]]
    when: NotRequired[Callable[[ToolCallRequest], bool]]  # new
```

When provided, `when` is called before adding a tool call to the batch interrupt. If it returns `False`, the call is auto-approved and excluded. If it returns `True` (or `when` is absent), existing behaviour is unchanged.

The predicate receives a `ToolCallRequest` with:
- `tool_call` — the raw tool call dict (name, args, id)
- `tool` — `None` (no `BaseTool` instance is available at the `after_model` stage)
- `state` — current agent state
- `runtime` — a `ToolRuntime` constructed from the node-level `Runtime`, with `tool_call_id` populated

Example:

```python
HumanInTheLoopMiddleware(
    interrupt_on={
        "delete_file": InterruptOnConfig(
            allowed_decisions=["approve", "reject"],
            when=lambda req: req.tool_call["args"].get("path", "").startswith("/etc"),
        )
    }
)
```

This change is fully backwards-compatible — `when` is `NotRequired` and existing configs without it behave identically.

> This PR was developed with AI-agent assistance.

fix.title: Require `ctx` in `tool_for_tool_def` and fix the `FunctionToolset` retry budget

introducing.head: d7dd35b421a4eb9cc3fe4eeb35aca769537da7ff
introducing.sha_method: squash merge commit and its first parent
introducing.pr_title: Use the workflow-prepared `tool_def` in Temporal function-tool activities instead of re-running `prepare`
introducing.pr_body: Under Temporal, the tool-call activity for a static `FunctionToolset` listed the toolset's tools again: ```python tool = (await toolset.get_tools(ctx))[params.name] ``` `FunctionToolset.get_tools()` calls `await tool.prepare_tool_def(run_context)`, so every tool's [`prepare`](https://ai.pydantic.dev/tools-advanced/#tool-prepare) function ran a **second** time inside the activity, against the activity's deliberately limited `RunContext` — and the tool definition the workflow had already computed and the model had already seen was thrown away. ### Verified symptoms (same tool, same run) - workflow-side `prepare` saw `{'prompt': 'hello', 'conversation_id': 'conv-1', 'messages_len': 1}` - activity-side `prepare` saw `{'prompt': None, 'conversation_id': None, 'messages_len': 'UserError'}` - a `prepare` that returned `None` under that degraded context killed the call with a misleading error for something the user never did: `UserError: Tool 'my_tool' not found in toolset 'ts'. Removing or renaming tools during an agent run is not supported with Temporal.` - silent variant: a `prepare` that varies the description, schema, or `timeout` produced a *different* tool definition than the one the model was given, and `FunctionToolset.call_tool()` then used the activity-side `timeout`. Reproduced in the new test: with the fix reverted, `prepare` ran at run steps `[1, 1, 2]`, the model's second request saw the description from the *third* `prepare` call, and the workflow-side `timeout=0.01` was silently dropped so the tool ran to completion. ### The fix Do what the MCP path already does: ship the prepared `ToolDefinition` in `CallToolParams` (the field already existed and was passed as `None` here) and rebuild the tool from it inside the activity, instead of re-deriving it. `_mcp_toolset.py` uses `toolset.tool_for_tool_def(params.tool_def)`, so this adds the equivalent minimal primitive for function tools: `FunctionToolset.tool_for_tool_def(tool_def)` looks the tool up by name and returns a `FunctionToolsetTool` carrying that tool's `call_func`/`is_async`/`args_validator`, but with the **workflow-side** `tool_def` (and therefore its `timeout`). `get_tools()` now shares the same construction. `prepare` is not run inside the activity at all, so the fix holds regardless of which fields the serialized run context happens to carry. Preserved behavior: - if the named tool is genuinely gone from the toolset, the existing `UserError` still fires (now covered by a test, so its `# pragma: no cover` is gone) - a `CallToolParams` that arrives without a `tool_def` — only possible for an activity scheduled by a worker predating this change — still falls back to preparing the tool itself, so in-flight executions complete across a rolling upgrade - a `prepare` function that *renames* its tool keeps working. `FunctionToolset.tools` is keyed by the name the toolset holds the tool under while `tool_def.name` is the name the model sees, so `FunctionToolsetTool` now tracks the former and the workflow sends it alongside the `tool_def`; the activity resolves the renamed tool to its function without re-preparing. A payload without that name falls back to `tool_def.name`, which is the same thing for every tool that was never renamed It also means edits made to a static toolset's tool definitions *outside* the toolset — agent-level `prepare_tools`, the `SetToolMetadata` capability — now reach the activity too, instead of being replaced by the re-derived definition. Sending the tool definition adds it to each tool-call activity's input. That's no new serialization requirement: the same `ToolDefinition`s (metadata included) already cross the activity boundary in every model request's `ModelRequestParameters`, and the dynamic-toolset path already sends `tool_def` in these same params. ### Not fixed here `durable_exec/_toolset.py`'s `call_dynamic_tool()` has the same defect for `DynamicToolset`: it re-resolves the toolset and calls `get_tools()` inside the durable unit, ignoring the `tool_def` the params already carry (so it re-runs `prepare` and discards any outer capability's tool-def edits, e.g. `SetToolMetadata` or `prepare_tools`). It's shared by Temporal, DBOS, and Prefect, and a separate PR is reworking that function for argument validation, so it's deliberately left alone to avoid a conflict. I reproduced it end-to-end on Prefect to confirm it isn't Temporal-specific or merely a degraded-context artifact: `prepare` ran at run steps `[1, 1, 2]`, the model's second request saw the third `prepare` call's description, and the discovery-time `timeout=0.01` was dropped so the tool ran to completion instead of timing out. DBOS and Prefect have no analogue of the *static*-toolset defect, verified by runtime probe rather than inference: under both, `prepare` ran once per model step (`[1, 2]`) and the flow/workflow-side `timeout=0.01` was the one enforced inside the durable unit. DBOS never wraps `FunctionToolset` at all (`dbos/_durability.py::_wrap_leaf_toolset`, documented in `docs/durable_execution/dbos.md`) and `DBOS.step_id` is `None` inside the tool, confirming it runs in workflow code; Prefect hands the live flow-side `ToolsetTool` straight into its task (`prefect/_function_toolset.py`), and its MCP path does the same. Follow-ups filed from the same audit, both out of scope here: #6902 (a `@agent.toolset`-registered `DynamicToolset` is silently never wrapped by any durability capability, measured on Temporal and Prefect) and #6903 (the Prefect cache-key projection omits `metadata`, so two agent runs in one flow run share cached model *and* tool results). ### Docs `prepare` under durable execution wasn't documented. Added a short note to the Temporal "Agent Run Context and Dependencies" section: for a `FunctionToolset`, `prepare` runs in workflow code with the complete `RunContext` and the definition it returns is what the activity enforces; `DynamicToolset` tools are the exception because the toolset is re-resolved inside activities. ### Tests `tests/test_temporal.py` (all run and pass locally on a 3.13 venv; the file is module-skipped on 3.14): - `test_durability_static_tool_prepare_runs_only_in_workflow` — `prepare` runs exactly once per model step, all in workflow code; the model sees those definitions; and the workflow-prepared `timeout=0.01` is what the activity enforces (retry prompt `Timed out after 0.01 seconds.`). Fails on both assertions without the fix. - `test_durability_removed_tool_still_raises_user_error` — a tool really removed from the toolset mid-run still fails with the tool-removal `UserError`. - `test_durability_call_tool_activity_without_tool_def_re_prepares_tool` — the pre-upgrade payload shape still runs the tool. - `test_durability_prepare_renamed_tool_runs_in_activity` — a `prepare` function that renames its tool resolves to the registered function inside the activity, and the model only ever sees the renamed tool. This path had no coverage at all before. Runs sandboxed, so the workflow's `prepare` result reaches the activity over the wire rather than through shared module state; without the name threading it fails with `Tool 'exposed_tool' not found in toolset 'renaming_ts'`. - No linked issue: found while auditing the durable-execution tool-call path. Happy to file one if maintainers prefer. ### Checklist - [ ] Any **AI generated code** has been reviewed line-by-line by the human PR author, who stands by it. - [x] No **breaking changes** in accordance with the [version policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/version-policy.md). - [x] **PR title** is fit for the [release changelog](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/releases).

pairs.confirm_note: The new helper that rebuilds a function tool from a prepared definition fell back to a hardcoded retry budget of one, while the normal tool listing fell back to the run context's budget, so the rebuilt tool could get the wrong retries. The fix requires the context and uses its budget.
pairs.scope_reason: Inconsistent default between two paths in the added code.

introducing.pr_body:
Closes #36957

---

With a checkpointer, `_build_commands` only wrote `structured_response` into state when the model call produced one, so a value persisted from a prior turn stuck around in the checkpoint. The routing edges (`_make_model_to_tools_edge`, `_make_model_to_model_edge`) only checked `"structured_response" in state` (key presence), so a turn whose first model call failed structured-output validation and needed a retry would exit the loop early using the previous turn's stale value instead of continuing to retry.

Fixes #36288

Anthropic have added support for [adaptive thinking](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/adaptive-thinking) for Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6. With this addition, `thinking.type: "enabled"` and `budget_tokens` are deprecated in favor of `thinking.type: "adaptive"`.

We update `ChatAnthropic` to treat `"adaptive"` the same as `"enabled"` in all code paths that check the thinking type (structured output, token counting, etc.).

Validation:
- Added unit tests for adaptive thinking (invoke, streaming, structured output)
- All existing tests continue to pass

Unit tests were written with AI assistance (Claude Code).

pairs.confirm_note: The fix handles newly released models that reject forced tool choice; the adaptive-thinking PR was correct for the models it targeted.

introducing.pr_title: Add response-based fallback support for `FallbackModel`
introducing.pr_body:
## Summary

Extends `FallbackModel`'s `fallback_on` parameter to support response-based fallback (non-streaming).

Closes #3640

## Motivation

Some models return successful HTTP responses but indicate failure in the response content. For example, Google's `WebFetchTool` returns `URL_RETRIEVAL_STATUS_FAILED` instead of throwing an exception. The existing exception-based fallback can't handle these cases.

## Changes

**Unified `fallback_on` API:**
The `fallback_on` parameter now accepts:
- A tuple of exception types: `(ModelAPIError, RateLimitError)` (backward compatible)
- A single exception type: `ModelAPIError` (backward compatible)
- An exception handler (sync or async): `lambda exc: isinstance(exc, MyError)` (backward compatible)
- A response handler (sync or async): `def check(r: ModelResponse) -> bool` (new)
- A list mixing all of the above: `[ModelAPIError, exc_handler, response_handler]` (new)

Handler type is auto-detected by inspecting type hints on the first parameter:
- If the first parameter is hinted as `ModelResponse`, it's a response handler
- Otherwise (including untyped handlers and lambdas), it's an exception handler

**Scope:**
- Non-streaming: Full support for both exception and response-based fallback
- Streaming: Exception-based fallback for initialization errors, plus response-based fallback after stream consumption (raises `ResponseRejected` in `FallbackExceptionGroup`; no transparent retry since events are already consumed)

**Documentation:**
- Added finish reason example showing response-based fallback on bad `FinishReason`
- Added built-in tool failure example with Google's `WebFetchTool`
- Added mixed handler example combining exception types and response handlers
- Added warnings explaining that a solo response handler replaces the default `(ModelAPIError,)` exception fallback
- Added per-model settings example showing provider-specific `ModelSettings`

**Code organization:**
- Moved `get_first_param_type` helper from `_utils.py` to `_function_schema.py` to keep Pydantic internal API usage contained

**Error handling improvements:**
- `FallbackExceptionGroup` now includes rejected responses in its error message
- Warning when `fallback_on` is empty (prevents silent misconfiguration)

## Example

```python
from pydantic_ai.messages import ModelResponse
from pydantic_ai.models.fallback import FallbackModel
from pydantic_ai.exceptions import ModelAPIError


def web_fetch_failed(response: ModelResponse) -> bool:
    """Check if a web_fetch built-in tool failed."""
    for call, result in response.builtin_tool_calls:
        if call.tool_name == 'web_fetch':
            # inspect result.content for failure indicators
            return True
    return False


# Auto-detected as response handler via ModelResponse type hint
fallback_model = FallbackModel(
    'google:gemini-2.5-flash',
    'anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-5',
    fallback_on=web_fetch_failed,
)

# Or mix with exception types for both exception and response fallback
fallback_model = FallbackModel(
    'google:gemini-2.5-flash',
    'anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-5',
    fallback_on=[
        ModelAPIError,
        lambda exc: 'rate limit' in str(exc).lower(),
        web_fetch_failed,  # Auto-detected via type hint
    ],
)
```

## Test plan

- 44 tests covering exception, response, and mixed fallback
- Both streaming and non-streaming scenarios
- Type hint auto-detection tests (including callable classes and forward references)
- Edge cases: exception propagation, empty handler warning, rejected response error messages

introducing.pr_title: Expose the message-history repair pipeline as `repair_messages`
introducing.pr_body:
- Closes #5637

The pipeline that makes a message history provider-valid — drop orphaned tool results, synthesize a return for each dangling tool call, merge adjacent compatible messages — lived in `_agent_graph` and ran only inside a run. It is already reached for from outside:

- `pydantic_ai/durable_exec/temporal/_model.py` imported `_clean_message_history` through a `# pyright: ignore[reportPrivateUsage]`;
- the Harness `StepPersistence` capability ships [its own copy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai-harness/blob/main/pydantic_ai_harness/step_persistence/_helpers.py) of the same call/result walk to gate snapshot writes.

This moves the passes **verbatim** to `messages.py`, where they belong — they are pure `list[ModelMessage] -> list[ModelMessage]` transforms over message types, with no dependency on the graph — and adds a public wrapper beside `sanitize_messages`:

```python
def repair_messages(
    messages: Sequence[ModelMessage], *, repair_last_response: bool = True
) -> list[ModelMessage]: ...
```

The first commit is the move plus the wrapper; the internals keep their names, so the graph's call sites are unchanged and the diff there is an import.

### What it unblocks

The repair runs before every model request, so a history handed to `Agent.run` is already fixed up and this is not needed for the normal path. The exception is a **new user prompt on top of a history whose last response still has unanswered tool calls**, which raises:

```
UserError: Cannot provide a new user prompt when the message history contains unprocessed tool calls.
```

That is deliberate — those calls can still be answered, by resuming the run or with `deferred_tool_results`, and closing them out silently would abandon work the caller may still want. But the message named no way forward. It now names all three, including `repair_messages()` for when abandoning them is what you meant. `repair_last_response=True` is the default for exactly that reason; pass `False` to repair everything except the live frontier.

### On the issue's open question: one function, not two

#5637 asks for `is_provider_valid(messages) -> bool` and asks whether a `repair` variant should come too. This ships the repair variant only, deliberately:

- The repair is idempotent and returns the input unchanged when there is nothing to do, so a caller who would have branched on the predicate can just repair — which is what the in-tree callers want. The Harness gate gets a *better* outcome from repairing before it records a snapshot (always resumable) than from declining to record one.
- The predicate cannot be derived from the repair, so shipping both would mean shipping two implementations. `repair_messages(m, repair_last_response=False) == list(m)` looks like it would work, and does for the cases that matter — but it also reports a perfectly valid history of two adjacent `ModelRequest`s as invalid, because merging them is normalization, not repair:

  ```
  good history                  -> True
  dangling tool call            -> False
  orphaned tool result          -> False
  two adjacent ModelRequests    -> False   # valid, just not normalized
  ```

If the standalone predicate is still wanted, say so and it can be a second PR that checks pairing only — it should not be a wrapper around this.

### Also here

The docs warning about slicing a message history has been wrong since the repair pipeline landed:

> **Be careful when slicing the message history** — you need to make sure that tool calls and returns are paired, otherwise the LLM may return an error.

A slice that separates a call from its result no longer reaches a provider that way. What it actually costs is content, silently: an orphaned result is dropped, and an unanswered call gets a synthesized `'interrupted'` return. The note says that now.

`SYNTHESIZED_TOOL_RETURN_METADATA_KEY` moves to `pydantic_ai.messages` with the rest of the pipeline, so the marker that tells a synthesized return from a real one is importable from where the parts themselves live.

- [x] No **breaking changes** in accordance with the [version policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/version-policy.md).
- [x] Any permitted **compatibility impact** has a label, warning, migration, release note, and exact API-check waiver.
- [x] **PR title** is fit for the [release changelog](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/releases).

- Introduced the `TemporalProviderFactory` type and support for passing a provider factory to Temporal agents and models, enabling custom provider instantiation logic (e.g., injecting API keys from dependencies) when resolving models from provider strings. (`pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/durable_exec/temporal/_agent.py`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-190f8dc438fdab2b98b4f4d9705e01f01749994ad76f7606439d83f81fa7469eL42-R42) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-190f8dc438fdab2b98b4f4d9705e01f01749994ad76f7606439d83f81fa7469eR60-R61); `pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/durable_exec/temporal/_model.py`, [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-af1e30880d85674edef6dd539047fd47bc806af40fb06050c46c5d3f744d54caL36-R39) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-af1e30880d85674edef6dd539047fd47bc806af40fb06050c46c5d3f744d54caR81-R112)

**Model selection logic in Temporal model activities:**

- Updated the Temporal model wrapper to support runtime model selection, including a context variable for the current model selection and logic to resolve the correct model instance for each request or stream activity. This ensures the correct model is used for each workflow step, whether by registered name or provider string. (`pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/durable_exec/temporal/_model.py`, [pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/durable_exec/temporal/_model.pyR81-R112](diffhunk://#diff-af1e30880d85674edef6dd539047fd47bc806af40fb06050c46c5d3f744d54caR81-R112))

- Introduced the `CURRENT_RUN_CONTEXT` context variable to track the current run context across asynchronous boundaries, and updated agent graph methods to set and reset this variable during model requests and streaming. (`pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/_run_context.py`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c062902ac73b2188a1b50b70289d314aa6c1c520f348203fc6d9c39022a40557R5) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c062902ac73b2188a1b50b70289d314aa6c1c520f348203fc6d9c39022a40557R75-R81); `pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/_agent_graph.py`, [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-71730070455237accebd709ba7fe41ce60edbd238af02e7d86a208cf8f10ab12R29) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-71730070455237accebd709ba7fe41ce60edbd238af02e7d86a208cf8f10ab12R441-R442) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-71730070455237accebd709ba7fe41ce60edbd238af02e7d86a208cf8f10ab12R462-R463) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-71730070455237accebd709ba7fe41ce60edbd238af02e7d86a208cf8f10ab12L471-R481)
